fullPassage:
[1번] Local elementary schools are invited to join us in celebrating the 25th anniversary of the city's subway system. We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the celebration. The theme of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be creative and show us what the subway means to you and your community. Each student may submit only one poster by September 22. This event is less about competition than it is about showcasing community spirit. However, the winner will receive a special subway tour, and the winner's school will receive $500. There will also be a promotional photoshoot featuring the winner and all of the winner's classmates. The judging period will take no longer than one week. So we expect to announce a winner by October 1. We hope everyone participates!

[2번] Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.

[3번] Hoarding disorder is a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive acquisition," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior tends to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy, which helps hoarders make better decisions about keeping or getting rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be required.

[4번] Have you ever seen rows of identical fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources growing unwanted produce.

[5번] Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that uses the palm of a person's hand as a unique form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is added to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need to carry credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.

[6번] It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.

[7번] Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an unconscious bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.

[8번] Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) special=특별한 / ordinary=평범한 (B) featuring=특별히 포함하는 / excluding=제외하는 (C) announce=발표하다 / cancel=취소하다
det.analysis:
① ordinary — featuring — announce: (A) 우승자에게 주는 상은 '평범한'이 아니라 '특별한'(special) 투어
② special — excluding — cancel: (B) 사진 촬영은 우승자와 반 친구를 '제외'가 아니라 '특별히 포함'(featuring) (C) 우승자를 '취소'가 아니라 '발표'
③ special — featuring — announce: '특별한' 투어 상, 우승자를 '포함'한 촬영, 우승자 '발표' ←정답
④ ordinary — excluding — cancel: (A)(B)(C) 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: '특별한'(special) 상, 우승자를 '포함'(featuring)한 촬영, 우승자 '발표'(announce)로 이어지는 흐름

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 narrow와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: narrow=좁은 / deep=깊은 / short=짧은 / empty=텅 빈 / broad=넓은
det.analysis:
① deep: 깊은 — 깊이 축의 다른 오답
② short: 짧은 — 길이 축의 다른 오답
③ empty: 텅 빈 — 의미축이 다른 오답
④ broad: 넓은 — narrow(좁은)의 반의어 ←정답

questions.passage:
(A) The word "excessive" here <u>means</u> far more than what is normal or healthy for a person to want or to keep at home.

(B) For students who live far from town, a bicycle is often the only <u>means</u> of getting to school safely each and every morning.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 means의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: means: (A) (뜻이) ~을 의미하다 (B) 수단, 방법
det.analysis:
① (A) 의미하다 (B) 수단: (A)는 단어의 뜻을 풀이하는 동사 '의미하다', (B)는 학교에 가는 '수단(방법)' ←정답
② (A) 수단 (B) 의미하다: (A)를 '수단'으로 보면 단어 뜻 설명과 맞지 않음
③ (A) 의미하다 (B) 의미하다: (B)는 이동 '수단'이라 '의미하다'가 아님
④ (A) 수단 (B) 수단: (A)가 부적절
det.tip: means의 다의어: 뜻을 풀이하는 '의미하다' vs 목적을 이루는 '수단'

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① perfect=완벽한 ② increasing=증가시키는 ③ absorbs→reflects (부적절) ④ changing=바꾸는
det.analysis:
① perfect: 사막은 태양광 발전에 완벽한 곳 — 적절
② increasing: 지구 평균 기온을 증가시킴 — 적절
③ reflects: 어두운 물이 해빙보다 태양 에너지를 더 많이 '반사(reflects)'한다? 어두운 물은 에너지를 더 '흡수(absorbs)'해서 온난화를 가속하므로 부적절 ←정답
④ changing: 강수 패턴을 바꿔 문제를 일으킴 — 적절
det.tip: 어두운 물은 에너지를 absorbs(흡수). reflects(반사)는 정반대라 온난화 논리와 모순

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 devised와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: devised=고안했다 / created=만들어냈다 / canceled=취소했다 / followed=따랐다 / delayed=미뤘다
det.analysis:
① created: 만들어냈다 — devised의 동의어 ←정답

③ followed: 따랐다 — 의미 다름

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the day on which an important event happened in a previous year, especially one that is celebrated or remembered every year"

det.korean: ceremony=의식, 식 / festival=축제 / memory=기억 / anniversary=기념일

③ memory: 기억 — 날짜가 아니라 마음속 기억
④ anniversary: 지난해 있었던 중요한 일을 해마다 기념·기억하는 날 = 기념일 ←정답
det.tip: 매년 돌아오는, 특정 사건을 기념하는 날 = anniversary(기념일)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) higher=더 높은 / lower=더 낮은 (B) strong=센 / weak=약한 (C) faster=더 빠른 / slower=더 느린
det.analysis:
① higher—strong—faster: 높이 올라갈수록 바람이 셈 + 센 바람이 건물을 침 + 좁을수록 더 빠름 ←정답
② lower—weak—faster: (A)(B) 높이 올라갈수록 '더 낮은'·'약한'이 아니라 더 높고 센 바람
③ higher—weak—slower: (B)(C) 문맥과 반대
④ lower—strong—slower: (A)(C) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 높이 올라갈수록 higher(더 높은)·strong(센) 바람, 통로가 좁을수록 faster(더 빠름)

det.korean: ① extreme=극심한 ② significant→trivial (부적절) ③ behavioral=행동의 ④ belongings=소지품
det.analysis:
① extreme: 저장 행동은 점점 극심해짐 — 적절
② trivial: 저장 행동이 '사소한(trivial)' 문제가 되면 치료한다? 본문은 '상당한(significant)' 문제가 되면 치료한다고 했으므로 반대 ←정답
③ behavioral: 행동 치료로 치료됨 — 적절
④ belongings: 소지품을 유지할지 버릴지 결정을 도움 — 적절
det.tip: 치료가 필요한 것은 significant(상당한) 문제가 되었을 때. trivial(사소한)은 반대

det.korean: ① identical=똑같은 ② wasted=낭비되는 ③ good→bad (부적절) ④ protect=보호하다
det.analysis:
① identical: 진열대에 줄지어 놓인 '똑같은' 과일 — 적절

④ protect: 환경을 '보호'하는 데 도움 — 적절
det.tip: 낭비된 농산물도 맛은 마트 것만큼 좋다(good). bad(나쁜)는 정반대

det.korean: identification=신원 확인 / entertainment=오락 / transportation=교통 / decoration=장식
det.analysis:
① identification(신원 확인): 손바닥을 사람을 알아보는 '고유한 신원 확인' 수단으로 쓴다는 흐름 ←정답
② entertainment(오락): 생체 인식과 무관
③ transportation(교통): 문맥 부적절
④ decoration(장식): 문맥 부적절
det.tip: a unique form of ___(고유한 ~ 수단) → identification(신원 확인)

questions.passage: It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have (A)[beneficial / adverse] environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would (B)[raise / lower] local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which (C)[reflects / absorbs] greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) adverse=부정적인 / beneficial=이로운 (B) raise=올리다 / lower=낮추다 (C) absorbs=흡수하다 / reflects=반사하다
det.analysis:
① beneficial—raise—absorbs: (A) 'Unfortunately' 뒤라 부정적 영향이므로 beneficial(이로운)이 아니라 adverse(부정적인)
② adverse—lower—reflects: (B) 사막을 태양광 패널로 덮으면 기온을 '올리므로(raise)' lower(낮추다)는 반대
③ adverse—raise—absorbs: 부정적 영향 + 기온을 올림 + 어두운 물이 에너지를 더 많이 흡수함 ←정답
④ beneficial—lower—reflects: 세 곳 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: Unfortunately → adverse(부정적) / 사막을 덮으면 기온 raise(상승) / 어두운 물은 에너지 absorbs(흡수)

questions.passage: Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an unconscious __________ that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: talent=재능 / bias=편견 / rule=규칙 / fact=사실
det.analysis:
① talent: 재능? 전 세계에서 무의식적으로 일어나는 것은 재능이 아님
② bias: 무의식적인 '편견(bias)'이 전 세계에서 일어남 ←정답
③ rule: 규칙? 무의식적으로 일어나는 성향과 다름
④ fact: 사실? 뒤에서 과소·과대평가라는 왜곡을 말하므로 '편견'이 적절
det.tip: unconscious ___ that occurs across the world → bias(편견)

questions.passage: Coral reefs are being __________ (threaten) by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: threaten(위협하다) → threatened. 'be being + 과거분사'(진행 수동태) '~되고 있는 중이다'
det.analysis: threaten을 과거분사 threatened로 바꿔요. 'are being threatened'는 'be동사 + being + 과거분사(p.p.)' 형태의 진행 수동태로 '위협받고 있는 중이다'라는 뜻이에요. 산호초가 따뜻한 물에 의해 '위협을 당하는' 쪽(수동)이라서 과거분사(threatened)를 써요.
det.tip: be being + 과거분사 = ~되고 있는 중이다. threaten → threatened

questions.passage: The theme of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be __________ (create) and show us what the subway means to you and your community.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: create(동사: 만들다) → creative. be동사(Be) 뒤 보어 자리이므로 형용사형
det.analysis: create를 형용사 creative로 변환. 'Be creative'는 '창의적이 되어라'라는 명령문으로, be동사 뒤에는 형용사(보어)가 와야 하므로 형용사형 creative가 필요해요.
det.tip: Be __________ 구조 = be동사 뒤 형용사 보어 → creative

questions.passage: This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water __________ (flow) in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: flow(동사: 흐르다) → flowing (명사 water를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사)
det.analysis: 명사 water(물) 바로 뒤에서 '흐르고 있는'이라는 뜻으로 물을 꾸며 주려면 동사 flow에 -ing를 붙인 현재분사 flowing으로 써요. water (that is) flowing in a river = 강에서 흐르고 있는 물처럼, 이렇게 앞의 명사를 꾸미는 분사예요.
det.tip: 명사(water)를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사 → water flowing in a river

questions.passage: Hoarding behavior tends to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is __________ (general) treated with behavioral therapy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: general(형용사: 일반적인) → generally(부사: 일반적으로, 보통). 뒤의 동사 treated를 꾸미는 부사 자리
det.analysis: 형용사 general을 부사 generally로 바꿔요. 'it is __________ treated'에서 빈칸은 뒤의 동사 treated(치료되다)를 꾸미는 자리예요. 동사를 꾸미는 것은 부사이므로 generally(일반적으로)가 맞아요. '보통 행동 치료로 치료된다'는 뜻이에요.
det.tip: 동사(treated)를 꾸미는 자리 → 부사 generally(-ly)

questions.passage: In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. __________ (fortunate), this is beginning to change.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: fortunate(형용사: 다행인) → Fortunately(부사: 다행스럽게도). 문장 전체를 꾸미는 부사 자리
det.analysis: 형용사 fortunate를 부사 Fortunately로 바꿔요. 문장 맨 앞에서 콤마로 이어지며 문장 전체를 꾸미는 자리는 부사 자리예요. 형용사에 -ly를 붙이면 부사가 돼요. 'Fortunately, ~' = '다행스럽게도, ~'.
det.tip: 형용사 + -ly = 부사 → fortunate → Fortunately (문장 전체 수식)
